branch_identification_note.title: Hohmann bridge parameter and branch identification
branch_identification_note.status: closed: the coverage obligation below is resolved by an independent global-uniqueness result for the minimizer, combined with the branch-identification arguments already in place at both junctions
branch_identification_note.text: The Hohmann bridge is certified directly in the auxiliary parameter t, with a determined by the regularized stationary equation Ghat(t,a) = 0. The proof of the sign H > 0 on this bridge is performed tile by tile in the (t,a)-domain. It does not rely on monotonicity or injectivity of the map t -> w = sqrt(p). At each of the 97 internal tile boundaries, the junction check certifies Ghat_a > 0 on the hull of the two adjacent a-intervals. Since each tile supplies a root in that hull, strict monotonicity implies that the two roots coincide. Thus the tilewise roots define a single consistently identified root across the entire bridge. At the Hohmann/central junction, branch identification is established independently by a direct overlap in (p,phi): both constructions provide a stationary root for every p in the certified overlap, and C_pphi > 0 on the corresponding product box gives uniqueness in phi. This junction argument does not use an image or monotonicity claim for w(t). Accordingly, the w-interval displayed for the Hohmann bridge is a descriptive endpoint label, not a claim that t -> w is injective or monotone.

closure.result: for every R > 1 and every phi in (0,pi), the stationary equation C_p(p,phi) = 0 has a unique root over the full physical domain p > 0, and that root is the global minimizer p*(phi,R). Consequently there is nothing for the certified Hohmann tile family to miss: on the phi-range it covers, the root each tile certifies inside its own (necessarily narrow) a-box is the only stationary point that exists anywhere on p > 0 for that phi, not merely the only one found by a local search.
closure.source: circular/existence_uniqueness_minimizer/ (companion result cited in the manuscript, Section 3.4): README.md states the result and its status (scientific status PROVEN -- ANALYTICALLY, reproducibility status REPRODUCED, technical audit 2026-10-25); lemma1_closure_stationary_point.py carries the closure argument; lemma1_stress_test_2000_trials.py is an independent numerical cross-check, not itself a proof; assumption_H_proof.md, assumption_H_proof_certificate.py, assumption_H_independent_verification.py, and assumption_H_certificate.json (all in the same folder) carry the Assumption H dependency itself, see 'assumption_H_verification' below.
closure.proof_structure: with s := sqrt(p), w := R^(-1/2) in (0,1), u related to cot(phi/2)/s: (i) a prior unconditional result ('Assumption H', closed 2026-09-30, located and independently re-verified in this session -- see 'assumption_H_verification' below) gives C_ss > 0 at every stationary point of C(.,phi,R), for every R>1 and phi in (0,pi), with no restriction; (ii) this script closes the remaining boundary step: C_s(0+) has a finite, strictly negative limit, and C_s(s)/s -> 2u(1+w^2) > 0 as s -> infinity; (iii) a topological argument then shows that two zeros of C_s, both satisfying C_ss>0, would force a third zero with C_ss <= 0 strictly between them by continuity, which is impossible if C_ss>0 holds at every zero -- so at most one stationary point of any kind (minimum, maximum, or saddle in the one-dimensional sense) can exist; combined with (i)'s existence (intermediate value theorem, same two boundary limits), the stationary point is unique and is the global minimum.
closure.assumption_H_verification: the 'Assumption H' proof referenced above is now deposited in circular/existence_uniqueness_minimizer/ (it was not shipped there prior to this closure, which only cited it): assumption_H_proof.md (the full writeup), assumption_H_proof_certificate.py (sha256 c85503e99920ea68711b1875fbacc7c8d9f8d25c541a445ede67d493537bd82c; the external collaborator's algebraic certificate, all assertions pass) and assumption_H_independent_verification.py (sha256 69102b3170e29abac506e9e13884e8b7eeedf70c3218361af6aa5d05677cd5fc; a from-scratch reconstruction of every algebraic step directly from the manuscript's original S1, S2 formulas, not from the collaborator's already-substituted notation; confirms every identity used in the proof exactly, with no residual hypothesis). Both scripts were re-executed in this session. assumption_H_certificate.json in the same folder is the certification record for this dependency, including this cross-reference.
closure.notational_correspondence_check: existence_uniqueness_minimizer/lemma1_closure_stationary_point.py works in substitution variables (s, w, q, u) rather than the Hohmann bridge's native (p, phi, R, t). The identity of the underlying cost function was checked numerically rather than by a symbolic rewrite: S1(p,phi,R) and S2(p,phi,R) as built from physical orbital quantities in hohmann_build_Rta.py (velocities, eccentricity, in variables p and t, with phi(t) = 2*arcsin(sqrt(t))) were evaluated side by side with the substituted-variable S1, S2 of lemma1_closure_stationary_point.py (s = sqrt(p), w = R^(-1/2), q = cot(phi/2)) at 50-digit precision, at 9 points spanning R in [1.05, 5.0] (including R=2, the value used throughout this region's certificates) and t in (0,1): all differences were at the level of floating-point roundoff (~1e-50 to ~1e-49), i.e. zero within precision. This is strong numerical corroboration that the two scripts' cost functions are the same object, not an independent symbolic proof of that fact.
